proposals.evidence: DEDR1654 gives Tamil kuṭi (-pp-, -tt-), Malayalam kuṭikka, Kannada kuḍi/kuḍu and Kodagu kuḍi- (kuḍip-, kuḍic-) drink. These simple and ordinary participial/nominal survey forms retain that drink stem and documented inflectional bases; source vowel/voicing and final morphology are preserved. Possible causative kuḍisu forms and opaque auxiliaries are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5548 gives Tamil/Malayalam vēṟu/vēṟē different, Kannada bēṟe and Kodagu bōre, with reduplicated vevvēṟē separately. These survey vēre-vēre/bore-bore and vowel variants are distributive reduplications of that other/different stem; preserve source repetition, voicing and vowels rather than adding two etymon rows for grammatical reduplication. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4992 explicitly gives Tamil muḻu/muḻucu/muḻutu whole/all and Malayalam muḻuvan entire. These southern survey muḷu-/muru-/muyu-/musu-/mucu- forms retain that whole/entire family and its ordinary nominal endings, preserving source reflexes of the medial liquid. The explicitly questioned Gondi comparison is not used. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
